teams.heading: Farrell says Ireland are 'raising the standard' before meeting Fiji
teams.body: Ireland head coach Farrell called Friday's 30-point win over Argentina a 'good night at the office' and said the squad is clearer on the standard it wants. "I suppose it's raising the standard to be as good as we possibly can." The win moved Ireland top of the northern hemisphere table for at least 24 hours. It followed a 40-21 defeat by the All Blacks at Eden Park, Ireland's previous outing. Fiji are next on the schedule.

lead.why: The only NEW item in the shortlist, and it gives Fiji's next opponent's coach on-record comment on their standards ahead of the Fiji fixture.

teams.heading: George Furbank returns to England's side for Australia after injury-hit absence
teams.body: England's 23-man squad for Sunday's Nations Championship match with Australia has been confirmed, and Furbank's return is the headline change: the full-back has been out of the Test side since November 2024 through injuries and a bout of appendicitis in the July window. Fin Smith has been deemed fit to play after a scare in the build-up, having started each of England's past five outings at fly-half. Greg Fisilau, the Exeter Chiefs back-rower, is in the matchday squad and, according to Planet Rugby's selection review, in line to win a maiden cap.

lead.why: The confirmed 23-man squad is England's own selection news, and Furbank's return is the headline change.

teams.heading: Antoine Dupont captains injury-hit France, Kalvin Gourgues wins first start against Fiji
teams.body: Fabien Galthié named Antoine Dupont as captain at scrum-half for Saturday's match against Fiji in Lyon, with Romain Ntamack at flyhalf, their first start together at half-back since March 2025. Dupont wrestled the number nine jersey from Maxime Lucu, who drops to the bench. Kalvin Gourgues, who has come off the bench four times, makes his first start in midfield alongside Yoram Moefana. Emmanuel Meafou, Thibaud Flament, Matthieu Jalibert and Fabien Brau-Boirie were all sidelined for the November internationals.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell admits Ireland missed chance to be ruthless against Argentina
teams.body: Ireland had 59 per cent of the territory against Argentina yet did not score after the 55th minute, when Ronan Kelleher finished a rolling maul. Farrell's post-match verdict was blunt: "I think the story of the game is we missed a chance to be ruthless." He admitted the side must improve if they are to challenge at next year's World Cup in Australia, with Fiji up next and then the world champion Springboks.

lead.why: It is a fresh coach verdict on the Argentina win that goes to Ireland's own weakness, and it has not been run in an earlier edition.

teams.heading: Quesada calls Springboks' first half among best in recent times
teams.body: Italy's head coach said Saturday's Turin defeat came against the best team in the world, and that South Africa's first half was among the best played in recent times. He credited his forwards' finishing of phases and defence on the driving maul. The kicking game and clearance kicks did not work, and in some situations Italy put themselves under pressure. The team got partly back into the match until the 70th minute, with more possession and a good try, and Quesada said the lessons matter before three important fixtures.

lead.why: Italy's own post-match coach analysis is new today and gives a different angle from the result already reported.

teams.heading: Sione Tuipulotu takes full responsibility for Scotland's discipline after All Blacks defeat
teams.body: Captain Sione Tuipulotu has spoken of his own role in the second-half fade. Sin-binned on 50 minutes, he said: "Our discipline wasn't good enough, and it starts with me. I got sent to the bin and 10 minutes with your captain off isn't good for any team. I take full responsibility for that." Scotland conceded 13 penalties to New Zealand's eight and scored nothing after the interval in the 43-21 Murrayfield defeat, with Tuipulotu admitting they were "nowhere near accurate enough" in that period.

lead.why: The most widely corroborated new item, and it gives Scotland's captain's own account of the defeat rather than another match report.

teams.heading: Josh Adams scores twice as Wales edge Japan 28-21 in Cardiff
teams.body: Wales survived a nervy finish to open their autumn campaign, with Steve Tandy's side made to sweat by Japan late on. Archie Griffin, the tighthead prop, opened the scoring after four minutes, and Louis Rees-Zammit ended an eight-Test tryless run with his first Welsh try of 2026 just before the break. Blair Murray's break from a loose Japan kick set up Tomos Williams for Josh Adams's second try, but a late Japan try brought the margin back to one score. Wales held on for a bonus-point victory.

teams.heading: Efraín Elías and Justo Piccardo yellow-carded as Pumas forward pack thins out
teams.body: Justo Piccardo was yellow-carded for offside on 34 minutes, leaving Argentina down to 14 men. Efraín Elías was later yellow-carded for a high tackle on Hugo Keenan, and Ireland's final try came against a seven-man Pumas pack. Leonel Oviedo also went off for a head injury assessment in the first half, returning after about four minutes. The 42-12 defeat was Argentina's third in four.

lead.why: A new Argentina-focused item on the Ireland match's forward-pack disruptions, covering yellow cards and an HIA rather than the Montoya head-injury story already reported.

teams.heading: Harry Wilson urges Wallabies to 'play our own game' against England
teams.body: Ahead of Sunday's opener at Twickenham, the captain said the Wallabies must be themselves: "We definitely want to be us." Wilson pointed to the 42-38 win over South Africa in Perth, when Australia scored five tries and backed their skills, even after being reduced to 11 men. He said the two New Zealand defeats, where the Wallabies conceded 93 points, had taught valuable lessons. Coach Les Kiss warned that England's back three "can do damage" if given space.

lead.why: It is the only new Australia item in the shortlist, and the other fresh pieces are about England or repeat stories already run.

teams.heading: Riku Kitahara started at fly-half for Japan in their defeat to Wales
teams.body: Japan went into Saturday's match in Cardiff without three of their first-choice fly-halves: Sam Greene and Seung-sin Lee were injured, and Ryunosuke Ito, who had started all of Japan's Tests in 2026, was back at university and missed the tour. Japan coach Eddie Jones gave the No. 10 jersey to uncapped Honda Heat fly-half Riku Kitahara, with Toyota's Shinya Komura, the only other fly-half on tour, on the bench. Komura's try four minutes from time made it a one-score game, but Wales held on for a 28-21 win.

lead.why: It is the only Japan selection story in the pack, and it explains who was missing from the fly-half position in the Cardiff defeat.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett brings up 50 Test tries against Scotland at Murrayfield
teams.body: Beauden Barrett's first try, his 49th in Test rugby, came off a Damian McKenzie flat pass and stretched New Zealand's lead to 24-14 in the first half. His second, two minutes after Josh Moorby's try following the break, brought up 50. Only Will Jordan has also reached that mark for the All Blacks. Their 43-21 win at Murrayfield on Saturday was their fourth straight in the Nations Championship.

lead.why: A new item with a fresh milestone (Barrett's 50th Test try) that the earlier editions have not covered.

teams.heading: Erasmus confirms Salmaan Moerat's late back spasms cost him Italy start
teams.body: Head coach Rassie Erasmus confirmed that lock Salmaan Moerat was replaced in the Italy starting XV after back spasms first flared on Thursday and returned in the warm-up. Moerat was due to make his first Test appearance of 2026, with Lood de Jager promoted into the side and Franco Mostert named among the replacements. "Salmaan's got back spasms," Erasmus told reporters, adding that he hoped the problem was not serious.

lead.why: It is a new, South Africa-specific fitness update on a named player, and it ahead of the France Test is more useful to a fan than the already-reported Italy match stories.
